newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Congressman asks probe of MI5.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Congressman asks probe of MI5.

text.p: A U.S. Congressman is calling for an investigation to determine if the British intelligence agency MI5 tried to discredit an aide to George Mitchell, President Clinton's envoy on Northern Ireland.

Representative Peter King, a New York Republican, said he wants to find out if MI5 was behind stories in the British newspaper the Mail on Sunday on Dec. 1 that alleged Martha Pope, an aide to Mitchell, had an affair with Gerard Kelly of Sinn Fein.
Pope said she never met Kelly.

King, in a letter he made public Wednesday to Secretary of State Warren Christopher said, "There is reason to believe the MI5 created this scandal in an effort to discredit Pope, and thereby Sen. Mitchell, and in effect, derail the entire Irish peace process.

"I am calling on you to demand that the British government conduct a thorough investigation of this incident and determine if its intelligence agencies were involved," King wrote Christopher. King is a frequent critic of the British government's policy on Northern Ireland.
"If MI5 was involved, the British government owes the American government a direct apology. If there was no MI5 involvement, the British government must state so unequivocally," he said.
